name: io.github.heavyblotto/caelus-mcp
description: 41-tool Caelus MCP for validated astrology: charts, transits, Vedic, facts, sky view, observation.

tools.name: natal_chart
tools.description: A person's birth chart. Requires their exact birth date+time and birthplace (all three: date, lat, lon). Use this — not current_sky — whenever the question is about someone's natal/birth chart. Returns 13 bodies (sun–pluto, chiron, nodes) with sign, house, retrograde, speed; ASC/MC; cusps; major aspects with orb, applying/separating phase, and strength (1=exact). Vs Swiss Ephemeris (1850–2150): Sun–Saturn ≤1″, Uranus ≤1.9″, Neptune ≤4.6″, Moon ≤2.5″, Pluto ≤3.4″ (Chebyshev pack), Chiron ≤1″, mean node ≤1″, true node ≤ 1′ vs SE's built-in ephemeris.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

house_system.description: House system (default placidus). Case- and spacing-insensitive; valid: placidus, whole_sign, equal, porphyry, koch, regiomontanus, campanus, alcabitius, morinus, meridian, polich_page, vehlow (aliases like "whole sign" also work).

separation.description: Aspect separation: 'longitude' (default, the zodiacal aspect) or 'spatial' (true great-circle separation accounting for ecliptic latitude — differs for the Moon, Pluto, and bodies far off the ecliptic)

output.description: 'float' (default) returns the usual floating-point payload. 'canonical' returns integers on a declared grid plus a sha256 digest: stable across machines/browsers/languages, hashable for caching and dedupe, precision-honest, with sign/house/aspects re-derived from the quantized values so displayed numbers and facts always agree

grid.description: Canonical grid (with output:'canonical'): arcsec (default), milliarcsec, centideg, dms ([deg,min,sec] triples), or accuracy (each body snapped to its measured validated accuracy — the most portable choice for cross-platform content addressing)

remainders.description: With output:'canonical': also return the remainder set — the integer sub-quantum residues quantization discarded, keyed by leaf path and bound to the payload digest. 'auto' picks one grid finer than the base; or name the refinement grid (must be strictly finer). Residues telescope: composeRemainders(payload, remainders) rebuilds the finer-grid payload exactly. Time residues are integer microseconds, distance residues integer nano-AU

tools.name: current_sky
tools.description: The sky at a moment and place — not tied to any person. Use for "what's the sky/transits right now" or the chart of a non-birth event. Date defaults to now; lat/lon default to 0,0 (geocentric on the equator at the prime meridian), where houses and ASC/MC are nominal — pass a real location if houses matter. For a specific person's birth chart use natal_chart instead. Returns positions, houses, retrogrades, aspects.

date.description: UTC ISO date-time (convert from local first); omit for now

lat.description: Latitude, north positive; default 0 makes houses nominal

lon.description: Longitude, EAST positive (Americas are negative); default 0 makes houses nominal

tools.name: sky_view
tools.description: Where the visible bodies land in a framed photo of the sky, for an image prompt. Give a place, a moment, an aim (compass direction and altitude), a lens, and an image size; get each in-frame body's pixel position, apparent size, brightness, the Moon's phase orientation, a sky-state summary (twilight, limiting magnitude, horizon row), the bright bodies just outside the frame, a ready-to-use prompt, and a machine-readable `renderPlan` (a body-free background-plate prompt plus the computed layers to composite locally, for a hybrid render pipeline). Caelus computes the geometry and photometry; it does NOT render the image. For "at sunset", first find the set time with sky_events, then pass it as date.

date.description: UTC ISO date-time (convert from local first); omit for now

elevation_m.description: Eye height above ground in meters (e.g. 9 for a third-floor window)

azimuth.description: Center compass direction: degrees from true north (east positive) or a 16-point name like "W" or "WNW"

altitude.description: Center altitude in degrees: 0 looks at the horizon, positive tilts up

lens.description: Lens preset; sets field of view and projection (ultrawide is fisheye, the rest rectilinear)

bortle.description: Dark-sky class, 1 (pristine) to 9 (inner city). Sets the night naked-eye limit and drives background star density and Milky Way visibility. Omit for a suburban default

deep_field.description: Pin the complete deep naked-eye star field (thousands of stars at exact pixels) instead of the bright catalog. Larger response; great for control images

overlays.description: Reference-frame overlays to project (annotations, not photoreal): the ecliptic line, the zodiac signs, house cusps and angles, and constellation figures. Exact pixels returned in `overlays`

include_stars.description: Include bright catalog stars when a star catalog is loaded

max_star_mag.description: Brightest-magnitude cutoff for stars (smaller is brighter); default 2.5, or the limiting magnitude when bortle is set

tools.name: sky_view_sequence
tools.description: A time sequence of sky frames for an animation: the same place, aim, and lens stepped through time. Returns a compact per-frame timeline (instant, twilight, Sun/Moon altitude, Moon phase + bright-limb, whether the Milky Way is in frame) plus the fixed celestial pole and the sky's sidereal rotation per frame. Each frame's full pixel-accurate spec comes from calling sky_view at that instant; this tool plans the timeline. Use for sunset-to-night transitions, star-trail planning, or Moon-phase progressions.

date.description: First frame, UTC ISO date-time; omit for now

azimuth.description: Center direction: degrees from true north or a compass name like "W"

tools.name: synthetic_validate
tools.description: Check an authored synthetic celestial system for ill-defined inputs: duplicate body ids, non-positive periods, out-of-range eccentricity, or a dangling observer. Returns `impossible` and a list of problems — the same honesty pattern as compileForm.

tools.name: synthetic_positions
tools.description: Positions of every body in an authored synthetic system at one instant. Three body modes: `placement` (fixed longitude), `periodic` (uniform motion), `kepler` (constant elements). With `observer` set on the system, positions are geocentric/apparent from that body (outer bodies can show retrograde). Pass `t_days` for abstract day units, or `date` (UT ISO) when body `epoch` values are Julian Days. Returns speed and retrograde per body.

date.description: UT instant as ISO 8601; used as t when t_days is omitted

t_days.description: Time in the same day units as each body's periodDays/epoch (abstract world frame)

tools.name: synthetic_sky_view
tools.description: Sky View for a mix of real and synthetic bodies: register the authored system on an ephemeral engine, then frame the visible sky like sky_view. Synthetic bodies can carry render attributes (sizeDeg, magnitude, color) that flow into the pixel spec and prompt. Real Sun/Moon/planets stay for twilight and context unless omitted from `bodies`.

date.description: UTC ISO date-time; omit for now

elevation_m.description: Eye height above ground in meters

azimuth.description: Center direction: degrees from true north or a compass name

bodies.description: Body ids to draw; defaults to Sun, Moon, planets, and every synthetic body

include_stars.description: Include catalog stars (usually off for fictional skies)

tools.name: transits
tools.description: Transiting planets vs natal chart: aspects within orb (applying/separating), natal house per transiting body.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

transit_date.description: UTC ISO date-time of transit moment (convert from local first); omit for now

tools.name: synastry
tools.description: Compare two people's birth charts: inter-chart aspects with orbs, house overlays both ways, plus ranked citable fact atoms and a ready `brief` (synastry/composite ids for auditCitations). Each person needs date+lat+lon. House overlays always use Placidus (not configurable here).

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

a.description: Person A birth data (UTC date, lat, lon)

b.description: Person B birth data (UTC date, lat, lon)

tools.name: find_aspect_dates
tools.description: Exact dates a transiting body makes an aspect, within a range: to a fixed longitude OR to another transiting body. Provide exactly one of target_lon / target_body. Includes retrograde re-hits. Body names are snake_case (mean_node, true_node).

target_lon.description: Fixed natal longitude in degrees. Provide this OR target_body, not both.

target_body.description: Another transiting body. Provide this OR target_lon, not both.

start.description: UTC ISO start date (convert from local first)

end.description: UTC ISO end date (convert from local first); range <= 50 years

zodiac.description: Zodiac for body and target_lon longitudes; tropical (default) or sidereal:<ayanamsa>

tools.name: rectification_grid
tools.description: Rectification sweep: ASC/MC at each step across a window of UTC hours on one date, with ASC sign-change times. Use when the birth time is unknown and you want candidate times. The sweep runs over window_start_hour..window_end_hour (UTC hours of the given date); the date's time portion is ignored.

date.description: Birth DATE (UTC) as ISO; only the calendar date is used, the time portion is ignored (the window_*_hour fields set the times swept)

window_start_hour.description: First UTC hour of the date to sweep

window_end_hour.description: Last UTC hour of the date to sweep

tools.name: sky_events
tools.description: Sky events in a UTC date range: rise/set/meridian transits (need lat+lon+body), lunar phases (new/quarters/full), solar and lunar eclipses, stations (body turns retrograde/direct; needs body), zodiac degree crossings (needs body + target_lon). Solar eclipses report global circumstances (type, magnitude, gamma) plus the greatest-eclipse location and path width; add lat+lon to also get local circumstances (type seen, magnitude, obscuration, contact times C1-C4). Lunar eclipses report type and magnitude; add lat+lon to learn whether the Moon is above the horizon there. Times to the second vs Swiss Ephemeris (stations to ~1 min: ill-conditioned by nature). Range <= 370 days.

start.description: UTC ISO start date (convert from local first)

end.description: UTC ISO end date; range <= 370 days

tools.name: planetary_hours
tools.description: Planetary hours for a moment and place: the unequal hour in effect (its ruler, day/night, hour number 1-24, start/end UTC), the ruler of the planetary day, and the full 24-hour ruler sequence. Hours split the day (sunrise to sunset) and night (sunset to next sunrise) into twelve each; the day ruler is the weekday ruler and the hours follow the Chaldean order. Needs lat+lon. Returns available:false above the polar circles when the Sun does not rise or set that day.

date.description: UTC ISO date-time (convert from local first); omit for now

tools.name: void_of_course
tools.description: Void-of-course Moon at a moment: whether the Moon makes no further Ptolemaic aspect to a traditional planet (Sun..Saturn) before it leaves its current sign. Returns the Moon's sign, the UTC time it exits that sign, and the UTC time of its next perfecting aspect (null when none remains -- i.e. void). Tropical by default.

date.description: UTC ISO date-time (convert from local first); omit for now

tools.name: returns
tools.description: Solar or lunar return: the instant(s) a body returns to its natal longitude within a window, plus the full return chart for the first one. The Sun returns about yearly (the solar-return chart for the year), the Moon about monthly. Return chart is cast for the return moment at return_lat/return_lon (defaults to the birthplace; pass the current/relocated place for a relocated return).

tools.name: progressions
tools.description: Secondary progressions (day-for-a-year) and solar-arc directions of a natal chart to a target date. Returns, per body, the secondary-progressed longitude and the solar-arc-directed longitude, plus the solar arc itself. Longitudes only (no houses), so no birthplace is needed.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

target_date.description: UTC ISO date to progress/direct to (convert from local first)

tools.name: composite
tools.description: Relationship charts for two people: the midpoint composite (each body and angle is the shorter-arc midpoint of the two natal positions) and the Davison chart (a real chart cast for the midpoint in time and place). Each person needs date+lat+lon.

a.description: Person A birth data (UTC date, lat, lon)

b.description: Person B birth data (UTC date, lat, lon)

house_system.description: House system (default placidus). Case- and spacing-insensitive; valid: placidus, whole_sign, equal, porphyry, koch, regiomontanus, campanus, alcabitius, morinus, meridian, polich_page, vehlow (aliases like "whole sign" also work).

tools.name: dignities
tools.description: Essential dignity and sect for the seven traditional planets at a moment and place. Per planet: its sign, any essential dignity (domicile/exaltation/detriment/fall), its weighted essential-dignity score (Lilly: rulership 5, exaltation 4, triplicity 3, term 2, face 1; detriment -5, fall -4) with a peregrine flag, its planetary sect (diurnal/nocturnal, null for Mercury), and whether it is in sect given a day or night chart. The chart is day when the Sun is above the horizon — so lat+lon are required.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

tools.name: lots
tools.description: The seven Hermetic lots (Arabic parts) — Fortune, Spirit, Eros, Necessity, Courage, Victory, Nemesis — cast from the Ascendant and reversing direction by sect (a chart is day when the Sun is above the horizon). Per lot: its longitude and zodiacal position. Lots are anchored to the Ascendant, so an exact time and lat+lon are required. Fortune and Spirit are mirror images about the Ascendant. Tropical by default.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

tools.name: profections
tools.description: Annual and monthly profections (a Hellenistic time-lord technique) at a target date. The natal Ascendant advances one whole sign per year of life; the profected sign's traditional ruler is the lord of the year, the single most important time-lord for that year. Returns the age in years, the month within the profection year, and the annual and monthly profected sign (with its whole-sign house from the natal Ascendant and its lord). Needs the birth time and place for the Ascendant.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

target_date.description: UTC ISO date to profect to (convert from local first)

tools.name: firdaria
tools.description: Firdaria (firdariyyat): the Persian/medieval planetary time-lord periods. Life divides into nine major periods totalling 75 years — the seven planets (a day chart starts with the Sun, a night chart with the Moon) then the North and South Nodes — each planetary period split into seven sub-periods. Returns the full timeline (each period and sub-period with UTC start/end) and, when target_date is given, the major and sub lord active then. Sect is taken from the birth chart, so lat+lon are required; pure time arithmetic, no zodiac.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

target_date.description: UTC ISO date to look up the active period for; omit for the timeline only

tools.name: releasing
tools.description: Zodiacal releasing (aphesis), the Hellenistic time-lord technique from Vettius Valens, released from a Lot (Spirit by default, or Fortune). From the Lot's sign, periods release sign by sign with planetary minor-year lengths on the 360-day-year convention; each level is a twelfth of the one above (L1..L4), and a loop back to the starting sign looses the bond, jumping once to the opposite sign (+6). Returns the timeline down to max_level over the horizon and, when target_date is given, the L1..L4 lords active then. Anchored to the natal Lot, so an exact time and lat+lon are required.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

target_date.description: UTC ISO date to read the active L1..L4 periods for; omit for the timeline only

lot.description: the Lot to release from (default spirit)

max_level.description: deepest sub-period level in the timeline, 1..4 (default 2)

horizon_years.description: timeline length in 360-day years from birth (default 100)

tools.name: directions
tools.description: Primary (mundane) directions of the seven traditional planets to the four angles (MC, IC, Ascendant, Descendant), and optionally between the planets themselves. The diurnal rotation carries a body to the angle (or a promissor to a significator); the arc of rotation, converted by a time key (Naibod 0.9856473°/yr by default, or Ptolemy 1°/yr), gives the age of the direction. Returns the directions within max_years, sorted by age, each with its arc, age in years, and UTC date. With include_mundane, also returns the planet-to-planet (promissor → significator) directions. Circumpolar bodies have no Ascendant/Descendant directions. Needs the birth time and place; equatorial, so zodiac is irrelevant.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

key.description: time key: naibod (0.9856473°/yr, default) or ptolemy (1°/yr)

max_years.description: only directions reached within this many years of life (default 90)

include_mundane.description: also return inter-planetary (promissor → significator) directions (default false)

tools.name: nakshatras
tools.description: The nakshatra (one of the 27 lunar mansions of 13°20′) of each classical point on the sidereal zodiac: the seven traditional planets and the Ascendant (lagna). Per point: the nakshatra name, its pada (quarter, 1–4), the ruling planet (the Vimshottari lord), and degrees into the nakshatra. The Moon's nakshatra (janma nakshatra) anchors the Vimshottari dasha. Sidereal by definition; Lahiri ayanamsa by default. Needs the birth time and place for the Ascendant.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

zodiac.description: sidereal ayanamsa (default sidereal:lahiri); these are sidereal techniques

tools.name: dasha
tools.description: Vedic dasha periods — planetary time-lord cycles started from the Moon's birth nakshatra. system selects Vimshottari (120-year, the standard), Yogini (36-year, eight yoginis), or Ashtottari (108-year). Returns the period timeline (mahadasha → antardasha) with UTC start/end, the balance of the first period at birth, and — when target_date is given — the lords active then (Vimshottari also gives the pratyantardasha). Sidereal; Lahiri by default. Needs the birth time and place.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

system.description: dasha system: vimshottari (120y), yogini (36y), or ashtottari (108y)

target_date.description: UTC ISO date to read the active lords for; omit for the timeline only

zodiac.description: sidereal ayanamsa (default sidereal:lahiri); these are sidereal techniques

tools.name: vargas
tools.description: Parashari divisional charts (vargas): the sign of each of the seven planets and the Ascendant in the requested D-charts — D1 rasi, D2 hora, D3 drekkana, D9 navamsa, D10 dasamsa, D12 dwadasamsa, D30 trimsamsa. Per point in each chart: the divisional sign and the division number within the rasi. The navamsa (D9) is the most consulted after the rasi. Sidereal; Lahiri by default. Needs the birth time and place for the Ascendant.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

zodiac.description: sidereal ayanamsa (default sidereal:lahiri); these are sidereal techniques

tools.name: yogas
tools.description: Vedic yogas (planetary combinations) on the sidereal rasi chart: the five Pancha Mahapurusha yogas (Ruchaka, Bhadra, Hamsa, Malavya, Shasha), Gajakesari, Budha-Aditya, and Chandra-Mangala; whether Kemadruma (the isolated-Moon yoga) is present; the raja yogas (a kendra lord associating with a trikona lord) and dhana (wealth) yogas, each as the lord pair and how they associate (conjunction, aspect, or exchange); and the chart's yogakarakas (a planet ruling both a kendra and a trikona). Sidereal; Lahiri by default. Needs the birth time and place.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

zodiac.description: sidereal ayanamsa (default sidereal:lahiri); these are sidereal techniques

tools.name: aspect_patterns
tools.description: Classical aspect configurations in a chart: T-squares, grand trines, grand crosses, yods, kites, mystic rectangles, and stelliums by sign and by house. Each is a structured object with the participating bodies and the worst defining-aspect orb; T-squares and yods also name the apex, stelliums their sign or house. Reported patterns are maximal — a grand cross hides the T-squares it contains, a kite its grand trine. Pure geometry (engine orbs plus a quincunx for yods), no interpretation. Needs date, lat, lon.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

house_system.description: House system (default placidus). Case- and spacing-insensitive; valid: placidus, whole_sign, equal, porphyry, koch, regiomontanus, campanus, alcabitius, morinus, meridian, polich_page, vehlow (aliases like "whole sign" also work).

tools.name: parans
tools.description: Parans (paranatellonta): co-angular bodies over the 24 hours from a date at a latitude — every pair of bodies simultaneously on one of the four angles (rising, culminating, setting, anti-culminating) within a stated tolerance. The relationship behind Brady's fixed-star parans, computed for the moving bodies; pure positional astronomy over the validated rise/set/transit times. Longitude-independent: latitude alone fixes the geometry, so only lat is needed. Date defaults to now.

date.description: UTC ISO date-time; the 24-hour window starts here. Omit for now

bodies.description: Bodies to consider; default the seven classical planets

tolerance_min.description: Paran window in minutes: the two angle crossings must fall within this gap

output.description: 'float' (default) returns the usual floating-point payload. 'canonical' returns integers on a declared grid plus a sha256 digest: stable across machines/browsers/languages, hashable for caching and dedupe, precision-honest, with sign/house/aspects re-derived from the quantized values so displayed numbers and facts always agree

tools.name: chart_signature
tools.description: A chart's structural signature as plain counts: element, modality, angularity, quadrant, and hemisphere distributions over the bodies; the dominant element, modality, and most-occupied sign; and the classical chart ruler (the ruler of the Ascendant's sign). Counts only, no interpretation — a compact summary for emphasis and comparison. Needs date, lat, lon.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

house_system.description: House system (default placidus). Case- and spacing-insensitive; valid: placidus, whole_sign, equal, porphyry, koch, regiomontanus, campanus, alcabitius, morinus, meridian, polich_page, vehlow (aliases like "whole sign" also work).

tools.name: chart_facts
tools.description:
A chart's validated facts as ranked, citable atoms for interpretation. Each fact has a stable id (e.g. "aspect:moon~neptune:conjunction"), the bodies it concerns, a salience score (luminaries, angular placements, the chart ruler, tight/hard aspects, configurations rank high), and a plain-language statement. Facts span placements, aspects, configurations, the structural signature, dispositors and receptions, a body's tight conjunction with a bright fixed star (e.g. "star:jupiter:Sirius"), and the Part of Fortune and Spirit (e.g. "lot:fortune"). Read the facts, write the interpretation in your own words, and cite the [id] each statement rests on — do not introduce facts not listed. Returns the ranked facts plus a ready-to-interpret `brief`.

By default a real birth chart: pass date+lat+lon. The chart's grounding is first-class via `realm` (what it is: observed/forecast/fictional/mythic/archetypal/…) and the time: an exact `date`, an uncertain `earliest`+`latest` range (the brief then frames it as provisional and trusts the Moon/angles/houses less), `constraints` for an archetypal chart with no time (synthesized via the compiler), or a full structured `when` (relative-to-another-event or a narrative calendar). A `when` of kind `relative` looks its `anchorId` up in `anchors` (a map of id → UTC instant supplied in the request). Omit lat+lon for a placeless chart (nominal houses).

date.description: Exact UTC instant, ISO 8601 (e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z); convert local to UTC first

earliest.description: Start of an uncertain-time range (UTC ISO); use with `latest` instead of `date`

latest.description: End of an uncertain-time range (UTC ISO)

when.description: Full structured temporal anchor; overrides date/earliest/latest. Use for relative or narrative time.

anchors.description: Reference instants for a `relative` when: { anchorId: UTC ISO }

calendars.description: Calendar lookups for a `narrative` when: { calendarName: { value: UTC ISO } }. The caller owns the mapping (a regnal year, a story epoch, a game calendar) — the engine resolves through it, never invents it

place.description: Named place, e.g. "Paris" or "Springfield, US" — resolved to a city centroid via the bundled gazetteer (GeoNames) when lat/lon are not given. Resolution is approximate by construction and reported as such

where.description: Full structured spatial anchor; overrides lat/lon and place. `fictional` carries the narrative value only — a fictional place never resolves to coordinates (the chart reads on the planetary layer, houseless), by design

realm.description: What the chart is; frames the interpretation (default observed)

constraints.description: Geometric constraints for an archetypal/conceptual chart with no time (compiler synthesis). Longitude kinds (aspect/sign/degree) plus the latitude-aware kinds: declination (via the fixed J2000 obliquity), parallel/contraparallel of declination, and separation3d (true great-circle separation)

house_system.description: House system (default placidus). Case- and spacing-insensitive; valid: placidus, whole_sign, equal, porphyry, koch, regiomontanus, campanus, alcabitius, morinus, meridian, polich_page, vehlow (aliases like "whole sign" also work).

target_date.description: UTC ISO instant for transits and time-lords vs this natal chart; omit for natal-only facts

include_vedic.description: With target_date: project nakshatra/varga/yoga (default true when zodiac is sidereal)

limit.description: max facts to return, highest salience first (default 24)

tools.name: counterfactual_chart
tools.description: A birth chart, perturbed — a 'what if'. Give a base chart (date+lat+lon) and an edit: `shift_time` (e.g. '1h', '-30m', 'P1D') moves the instant ("born an hour later"), `move_lat`+`move_lon` recompute at another place, and/or `set_longitudes` moves bodies to new ecliptic degrees ("Mars in the next sign"). Returns the diff vs the original: bodies that changed sign or house, aspects gained or lost, and angles that changed sign. A time/place edit rotates the houses and angles while planets stay put; a longitude splice moves only those bodies and recomputes their aspects.

date.description: UTC date-time, ISO 8601, e.g. 1990-06-10T14:30:00Z. Convert local birth time to UTC first.

move_lat.description: Recompute at this latitude instead of the birth latitude

move_lon.description: Recompute at this longitude instead of the birth longitude

set_longitudes.description: Move bodies to these ecliptic longitudes in degrees, e.g. { "mars": 45 }

house_system.description: House system (default placidus). Case- and spacing-insensitive; valid: placidus, whole_sign, equal, porphyry, koch, regiomontanus, campanus, alcabitius, morinus, meridian, polich_page, vehlow (aliases like "whole sign" also work).

tools.name: similar_skies
tools.description: Find when the sky most resembled a reference moment. Builds a feature vector for the reference date's planetary configuration and scans a window for the closest matches by cosine similarity (1.0 = identical configuration). Answers 'when did the sky last look like this?' for transit echoes and historical analogues. Returns the top matches with their similarity, highest first.

reference_date.description: UTC ISO date whose sky is the target to match

start.description: UTC ISO start of the search window

end.description: UTC ISO end of the search window

tools.name: electional_search
tools.description: Rank moments in a window for an electional aim. Samples the window and scores each instant by how closely a set of wanted body-to-body aspects is satisfied (tighter and applying aspects score higher), optionally penalizing a void-of-course Moon. Returns the top moments with the aspects that matched. Body-to-body only; for aspects to the angles, compute the chart at a candidate moment.

start.description: UTC ISO start of the window

end.description: UTC ISO end of the window

wanted.description: aspects to reward when close to exact

tools.name: cosmic_weather
tools.description: The mundane sky on a date: the active aspect configurations among the transiting planets (T-squares, grand trines, grand crosses, yods, kites, mystic rectangles, stelliums by sign), any planet stationing within a window, and whether the Moon is void of course. A 'cosmic weather' snapshot; no birth chart or location needed.

date.description: UTC ISO date

window_days.description: days either side to scan for stations (default 7)

tools.name: date_sky
tools.description: Date a described sky: find every window in a span of years in which a set of planetary positions held at once. The inverse of a chart, and the computation used to date a horoscope that records positions and no year. Each constraint puts a body in a zodiac sign, within an orb of a longitude, or in a from/to arc, or puts the elongation between two bodies in an arc (moon minus sun from 180 to 360 is a waning Moon). A constraint can instead be a first or last visibility at a place ('visibility': Venus first seen in the evening from Babylon, the heliacal rising of Sirius at Memphis, the new crescent), which holds on the days that event could have fallen on; give it together with at least one position, because alone it is slow over centuries. Returns the matching windows with calendar dates (Julian calendar before 15 October 1582) and a funnel showing how many windows survived each constraint, slowest body first. Years are astronomical: 0 is 1 BCE and -409 is 410 BCE. The searchable span depends on the server's data: a local stdio server with era packs covers about 3000 BCE to 3000 CE for the Sun, the Moon, and the planets through Pluto; a hosted server on the embedded tier covers 1000 to 3000.

body.description: body whose longitude is constrained, snake_case (sun, moon, mercury ... saturn)

elongation.description: two bodies [a, b]: constrains longitude of a minus longitude of b, instead of 'body'

sign.description: zodiac sign by name (e.g. 'Libra') or index 0-11

lon.description: centre longitude in degrees, used with 'orb'

from.description: arc start in degrees, used with 'to'

to.description: arc end in degrees, going forward from 'from'

pad.description: degrees to widen this arc on both sides

target.description: planet in snake_case, 'moon', or a catalog star name (Sirius, Regulus ...)

kind.description: which event, as in the heliacal tool

extinction.description: V-band extinction, magnitudes per air mass (default 0.25)

spread.description: half-width of the extinction range behind the event's window (default 0.05)

visibility.description: a first or last visibility at a place, instead of 'body' or 'elongation' and an arc

within_days.description: for 'visibility': days to widen the event's window on each side

constraints.description: what the sky looked like; every constraint must hold at once

start_year.description: first year to search, astronomical (negative for BCE: -409 is 410 BCE)

pad.description: degrees to widen every arc; use a few degrees when the source's zodiac is not the tropical one

tools.name: chart_stability
tools.description: What a chart still says when its time is uncertain. Given a date and time, an uncertainty in minutes, and optionally a place, reports which facts hold across the whole window (each body's sign, house, and direction, the signs on the Ascendant and Midheaven, day or night sect, and the aspects between bodies) and, for each fact that does not, the instants at which it changes. Use it when a birth time is rounded or approximate (15 for a quarter hour either way), or unknown (720 with the date at 12:00, which covers the whole day). Without lat and lon the angles, houses, and sect are left out. With no uncertainty given, the window is the clock error of the epoch (delta T), which only matters for dates centuries in the past.

date.description: UTC ISO date-time at the centre of the window

uncertainty_minutes.description: how far the true time may be from the stated one, either way, in minutes (max 720)

house_system.description: House system (default placidus). Case- and spacing-insensitive; valid: placidus, whole_sign, equal, porphyry, koch, regiomontanus, campanus, alcabitius, morinus, meridian, polich_page, vehlow (aliases like "whole sign" also work).

tools.name: heliacal
tools.description: First and last visibility of a planet, a star, or the Moon from a place: the heliacal rising (morning_first, the first morning a body is seen again before sunrise after its conjunction with the Sun), the heliacal setting (evening_last), the evening_first and morning_last of Mercury, Venus, and the Moon (evening_first for the Moon is the new crescent), and by the arcus method the acronychal_rising and cosmical_setting at opposition. These are the events ancient records report, and the dates depend on the place. The default method is a physical visibility model (sky brightness in twilight and moonlight, atmospheric extinction, the eye's threshold; Schaefer's published formulas), and the Moon's crescent uses Yallop's q test. Each event comes with an earliest and a latest date, the same event under a clearer and a hazier sky, because the haze on a given morning is not known. method 'arcus' is the classical geometric rule and needs arcus_visionis, the Sun's depression in degrees when the body is on the horizon. With no kind given, every event the target has is returned. Dates are the next occurrence at or after the start date; years are astronomical (0 is 1 BCE, -599 is 600 BCE) and the Julian calendar is used before 15 October 1582. target is a planet (mercury to saturn), 'moon', or a catalog star name such as Sirius, Regulus, Aldebaran, Spica, Antares.

target.description: planet in snake_case (mercury, venus, mars, jupiter, saturn), 'moon', or a star name (Sirius, Regulus, Spica ...)

start_year.description: year to search from, astronomical (negative for BCE: -599 is 600 BCE)

kind.description: which event; omit for every event the target has

arcus_visionis.description: for method 'arcus': the Sun's depression in degrees when the body is on the horizon

extinction.description: V-band extinction, magnitudes per air mass: 0.15 a clear mountain, 0.25 a clear sea-level sky (default), 0.35 and up hazy

spread.description: half-width of the extinction range behind 'earliest' and 'latest' (default 0.05)

altitude_m.description: observer height above sea level in metres

tools.name: verify_observation
tools.description: Verify physical observations (solar shadows, Sun/Moon azimuth and altitude, twilight regime, lunar illumination, waxing/waning phase, zenith-frame bright-limb angle, naked-eye planets, or video shadow sweep) against a claimed UTC timestamp and Earth location, or omit `observed` to query the full physical ground-truth scene (Sun, flat/sloped-ground 3D shadows, optional camera lighting and glare risk, Moon geometry and moonlight shadows, visible planets, diurnal sunrise/noon/sunset/twilight transitions, and compact chronosense context header). When `observed` is supplied, returns a verdict (`consistent`, `marginal`, `inconsistent`, `impossible`), consistency score, per-constraint residuals with automatic widening for `time_tolerance_min` and `place_tolerance_deg`, indeterminate handling for near-zenith shadows and full/new Moon bright limb, and counterfactual forensics (`time_shift`, `hemisphere_flip`, `date_shift`) whenever a claim fails. When `observed` is omitted, returns `verdict: 'unconstrained'` with the full physical `scene` and `chronosense`.

date.description: Claimed UTC ISO date-time (convert from local first); omit for now

elevation_m.description: Observer elevation above sea level in meters (adjusts barometric refraction and horizon dip; default 0)

slope_deg.description: Local terrain slope angle in degrees from horizontal (0..90; default 0 for flat ground)

slope_azimuth_deg.description: Downhill compass azimuth of sloped terrain in degrees clockwise from true north (default 0)

time_tolerance_min.description: Claimed timestamp uncertainty half-width in minutes; widens check tolerances by body motion rates (default 0)

place_tolerance_deg.description: Claimed location uncertainty radius in degrees; widens geometric tolerances (default 0)

bortle.description: Dark-sky class 1 (pristine) to 9 (inner city) for naked-eye planet visibility thresholds

camera_aim_az_deg.description: Optional camera compass azimuth in degrees clockwise from true north; enables camera-relative lighting and glare risk

camera_aim_alt_deg.description: Camera pitch angle in degrees above horizon (default 0)

prev_date.description: Optional previous UTC ISO timestamp; sets chronosense.night_crossed if local astronomical night elapsed since then

deadline_date.description: Optional target deadline UTC ISO timestamp; populates chronosense.deadline with remaining minutes and phase

shadow_bearing_deg.description: Compass bearing shadow points toward, degrees clockwise from true north (0=N, 90=E, 180=S, 270=W)

shadow_length_ratio.description: Shadow length divided by vertical object height (L/H, >= 0)

sun_azimuth_deg.description: Observed solar compass azimuth, degrees clockwise from true north

sun_altitude_deg.description: Observed apparent solar altitude above horizon in degrees

twilight.description: Lighting regime: day, civil, nautical, astronomical, night, daylight (day or civil), or dark (nautical through night)

sun_visible.description: Whether the Sun is visible above the horizon

moon_visible.description: Whether the Moon is visible above the horizon

moon_azimuth_deg.description: Observed lunar compass azimuth, degrees clockwise from true north

moon_altitude_deg.description: Observed apparent lunar altitude above horizon in degrees

moon_waxing.description: Whether the Moon is waxing (true) or waning (false)

bodies_visible.description: Celestial bodies reported visible in the scene

delta_bearing_deg.description: Signed compass change of shadow bearing over dt_minutes (+ clockwise, - counterclockwise)

shadow_sweep.description: Observed shadow rotation over a video or time-lapse interval

shadow_length_ratio.description: Override total shadow length ratio tolerance

shadow_length_ratio_abs.description: Absolute shadow length ratio tolerance floor (default 0.08)

moon_bright_limb_deg.description: Moon bright-limb zenith angle tolerance in degrees (default 18)

shadow_sweep_deg.description: Shadow sweep angle tolerance in degrees (default 5)

tools.name: chronolocate
tools.description: Find every UTC time window within a date range at a known location where a set of physical observations (shadows, solar or lunar azimuth/altitude, twilight, Moon illumination/waxing/bright-limb angle, visible planets, or shadow sweep) held simultaneously. Prunes impossible days analytically from solar and lunar declinations and phase, refines matching window edges to sub-second accuracy, and returns peak timestamps and fit scores. Use this to recover when a photo, video, or log entry was captured at a known place. Range <= 370 days.

end.description: UTC ISO end date-time of search range (convert from local first); range <= 370 days

tools.name: geolocate
tools.description: Invert physical observations at a known UTC timestamp to feasible Earth coordinates or regions. When flat ground and both solar direction (`sun_azimuth_deg` or `shadow_bearing_deg`) and solar elevation (`sun_altitude_deg` or `shadow_length_ratio`) are given, solves an analytical closed-form celestial navigation fix with damped Gauss-Newton refinement and covariance uncertainty radius (`method: 'analytical'`). For any other observable combination (Sun+Moon, bright-limb angle, twilight, visible planets, or sloped terrain), sweeps a global spherical grid with antimeridian-wrapping cluster refinement (`method: 'grid'`). Returns subsolar and sublunar ground points plus ranked candidate regions classified as `point`, `arc`, or `band`.

tools.name: chronosense_tick
tools.description: Compute a deterministic physical-horizon chronosense envelope for an agent turn at a UTC timestamp and Earth location, along with its compact plain-text header (`[CAELUS-CHRONO ...]`, zero astrological vocabulary), 10-D L2-normalized `photoperiodVector`, and unsupervised `phaseStratumKey` (`<horizon>:<season>:lon<0..5>`). Computes an 8-character canonical chart digest (`clockId`), explicit local solar-midnight `nightCrossed` flag, photoperiod-warped `daySlot` (`1..12` or `polar_day`/`polar_night`), separated horizon and deadline countdowns, and follow-the-sun `wavefrontQuadrant`. Pass the returned `envelope` directly to `audit_chronosense_cursor` to verify an agent's write-back cursor.

date.description: UTC ISO date-time for the current turn (convert from local first); omit for now

prev_date.description: Optional previous turn UTC ISO timestamp (computes nightCrossed and dtPrevMin)

deadline_date.description: Optional active task deadline UTC ISO timestamp

deadline_label.description: Optional short label for the active deadline (default 'deadline')

elevation_m.description: Observer elevation above sea level in meters (default 0)

tools.name: audit_chronosense_cursor
tools.description: Deterministically audit an agent's pre-tool write-back cursor and cited physical facts against the authoritative chronosense envelope. Accepts either an `envelope` object from `chronosense_tick` or recomputes the envelope directly from `{ date, lat, lon, turn, prev_date, deadline_date, deadline_label }`. Verifies `clockId` digest match, monotonic `turn`, explicit `nightCrossedAck` when local solar midnight elapsed, active `deadlineEtaMin` within `deadline_tolerance_min`, and optional `citedFacts` provenance within `fact_tolerance`. Returns `{ ok, driftFlags, correctivePrompt }`.

turn.description: Monotonic turn counter matching the authoritative header

nightCrossedAck.description: Must be true whenever night_crossed=true in the envelope

deadlineEtaMin.description: Signed minutes remaining to active deadline, or null when no deadline is active

citedFacts.description: Optional map of cited envelope fact keys to claimed values

cursor.description: Agent write-back cursor (accepts camelCase or snake_case keys)

envelope.description: Authoritative envelope object from chronosense_tick (camelCase or snake_case). Omit to recompute from date, lat, and lon.

date.description: UTC ISO date-time (required with lat and lon when envelope is omitted)

turn.description: Monotonic agent turn counter when recomputing envelope (default 1)

prev_date.description: Optional previous turn UTC ISO timestamp when recomputing envelope

deadline_date.description: Optional active task deadline UTC ISO timestamp when recomputing envelope

deadline_label.description: Optional deadline label when recomputing envelope (default 'deadline')

elevation_m.description: Observer elevation above sea level in meters when recomputing envelope (default 0)

genesis_digest.description: Optional session genesis chart digest when recomputing envelope

deadline_tolerance_min.description: Allowed drift in minutes for deadline_eta_min (default 5)

fact_tolerance.description: Allowed numeric tolerance for cited_facts provenance checks (default 0.5)
